title: opencode-village v2: distributable plugin with role redesign
description:
## Context

Repackage the current Agentic Village setup as a publishable npm plugin (`@technoch1ef/opencode-village`) and overhaul role design.

Current state:
- Plugin is a single 774-line file (`plugins/village.ts`) coupled to this user-config repo
- Roles: `mayor` / `worker` / `overseer` / `github` (standalone, not orchestrated)
- `overseer` rubber-stamps work without adding judgment value
- `github` agent is unrelated to village flow

Target state:
- Drop-in plugin: `npm i @technoch1ef/opencode-village` + `npx @technoch1ef/opencode-village init`
- Roles + handoff chain: **mayor → worker → inspector → guard → envoy (optional)**
  - `mayor`: clarify scope, create epic + child beads
  - `worker`: implement, local commit, hand off to inspector
  - `inspector`: judgment first — AC coverage, diff scope, regressions, stack review checklists. Returns to worker on issues, otherwise hands to guard
  - `guard`: mechanical checks — tests/lint/build/type/coverage. Returns to worker on red, otherwise closes (or hands to envoy if bead requests it)
  - `envoy`: optional, on-demand only — push, PRs, releases (only role with `git push` / `gh *`)
- New tools: `village_handoff`, `village_invoke`, `village_lint`, `village_board`, `village_detect_stack`, `village_worktrees`
- Hardened `village_claim` (worktree isolation)
- Hardened `village_scaffold` (bead linting, stack auto-injection)
- `/village:board`, `/village:envoy` commands

Why inspector before guard: judgment catches scope/AC issues cheaply before burning CI cycles on out-of-scope or under-specified work.

Non-goals:
- No `scribe` agent (out of scope)
- No backward compat with `overseer` / `github` agent names

## Skills

- beads-workflow

## Branch

\`epic/village-v2\`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child beads closed
- [ ] Plugin published as \`@technoch1ef/opencode-village\` on npm (or ready to publish)
- [ ] \`npx @technoch1ef/opencode-village init\` installs agents/commands/skills into a fresh \`~/.config/opencode\`
- [ ] README documents install + roles + commands + tools

## Notes

Branch \`epic/village-v2\` does not exist yet — create locally before workers claim children.

title: Worker creates epic branch on first claim; keeps it current with main/master
description:
## Context

Today workers are forbidden from creating branches (\`git checkout -b*\`, \`git switch -c*\`, \`git branch*\` denied in \`worker.md\`). This forces the human to manually create \`epic/<name>\` before any work can start, and the epic body has to carry a \"create this branch first\" warning.

Change: when a worker claims the first child of an epic, it should create the epic branch itself, rooted at the latest \`main\` or \`master\`, and keep it up to date on each subsequent claim.

This is the only branch-creation power a worker gets. They still cannot create arbitrary feature branches, push, or do destructive ops.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

\`epic/village-v2\`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \`assets/agents/worker.md\` permission updates:
  - ALLOW \`git checkout -b epic/*\` and \`git switch -c epic/*\` (only the \`epic/\` prefix)
  - ALLOW \`git fetch origin\` (read-only remote refresh, needed to know what \"current main\" is)
  - ALLOW \`git merge origin/main --ff-only\` and \`git merge origin/master --ff-only\` (fast-forward only — no merge commits, no conflict resolution by worker)
  - All other branch / push / non-ff-merge ops remain denied
- [ ] New tool \`village_ensure_branch({ branch: string, base?: \"main\"|\"master\"|\"auto\", directory? })\`:
  - Detects default base (\`auto\`): inspects \`git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD\` → falls back to checking \`main\` then \`master\`
  - Runs \`git fetch origin <base>\` (best-effort; no-op if no remote)
  - If branch does NOT exist locally:
    - If it exists on \`origin\`: \`git checkout -B <branch> origin/<branch>\`
    - Otherwise: \`git checkout -b <branch> origin/<base>\` (or local \`<base>\` if no remote)
  - If branch DOES exist locally:
    - \`git checkout <branch>\`
    - If clean working tree: \`git merge origin/<base> --ff-only\` (skip if non-fast-forward — return warning, do not error)
    - If dirty working tree: skip merge entirely, return \`dirty: skipping ff-merge\`
  - Returns structured result: \`{ branch, base, action: \"created\"|\"checked_out\"|\"updated\"|\"skipped\", warnings: string[] }\`
  - NEVER force-pushes, force-resets, or rebases
- [ ] \`village_claim\` integration:
  - After successful claim, parse \`## Branch\` from the bead body
  - If branch matches \`^epic/\`: call \`village_ensure_branch\` automatically
  - Append the branch result to the claim return value (so worker sees what happened)
  - On dirty-skip warning: surface clearly so worker knows to commit/stash before proceeding
- [ ] Worker prompt (\`assets/agents/worker.md\`) updated:
  - Step 3 (\"ensure you are on the bead's branch\") replaced with: \"village_claim has placed you on the branch and refreshed it from \`<base>\`; verify with \`git status\`\"
  - Add: \"If \`village_ensure_branch\` returned \`skipped\` due to dirty tree, commit/stash first then re-run via \`village_ensure_branch\`\"
- [ ] Update epic-bead body convention: \`## Branch\` may reference an epic branch that does not yet exist; mayor no longer needs to instruct human to pre-create it
- [ ] Update \`assets/agents/mayor.md\` step 4: REMOVE \"Ensure the local branch referenced by the epic exists\" — it's now automatic
- [ ] Unit tests cover:
  - First claim: branch created from \`origin/main\`
  - Subsequent claim: branch fast-forwarded
  - Dirty tree: skip ff-merge with warning, don't error
  - No remote: fall back to local base, no fetch failure
  - Non-fast-forward divergence: warn, leave branch as-is
  - Bead with non-\`epic/\` branch: \`village_claim\` does NOT auto-create

## Notes

Why ff-only and never rebase: the worker must not rewrite history that other workers/inspector/guard might have based commits on. If the epic branch has truly diverged from main (real conflicts), that's a coordination problem the human must resolve — surface it as a warning, do not silently merge.

Why only \`epic/*\` prefix is permitted: prevents workers from inventing their own branches mid-task. The branch namespace is still planned by the mayor in the bead body.

Order: this bead should land alongside or just after \`village_claim\` modularization (depends on opencode-2c6.2). It is INDEPENDENT of the inspector/guard split, so workers benefit immediately.

title: Add village_handoff tool + refactor agents to use it
description:
## Context

Replace the manual \`br comments add <id> "..." && br update <id> --assignee X --status open\` two-step with a single atomic tool.

Handoff chain: **mayor → worker → inspector → guard → envoy (optional)**.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

\`epic/village-v2\`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \`src/tools/handoff.ts\` exports \`village_handoff\` tool
- [ ] Schema: \`{ bead: string, to: "worker"|"inspector"|"guard"|"mayor"|"envoy", note: string, status?: "open"|"blocked" }\`
- [ ] Validates current actor (from session agent) is allowed to hand off to \`to\` (matrix below, enforced + documented in JSDoc)
- [ ] Posts standardized comment header: \`[handoff <from>→<to>] <note>\`
- [ ] Atomically updates assignee + status (single \`br update\` call)
- [ ] Returns updated bead summary line
- [ ] \`assets/agents/worker.md\` updated to use \`village_handoff\` instead of two-step
- [ ] \`assets/agents/inspector.md\` and \`assets/agents/guard.md\` use it (created in their own beads, this bead just guarantees the tool exists and is documented)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: valid handoff, invalid actor→target, missing bead

## Notes

Allowed handoff matrix (chain: mayor → worker → inspector → guard → envoy):
- worker → inspector (default after implementation)
- inspector → guard (judgment passed) | worker (changes requested) | mayor (out of scope)
- guard → worker (checks failed) | envoy (only if bead body explicitly requests release/PR)
  - guard does NOT hand off to inspector — guard closes the bead itself on green
- mayor → worker (rescope)
- envoy → (none; envoy closes or returns to guard with comment)

Closing happens at the end of the chain:
- guard closes on green checks (default terminal)
- envoy closes after merge (if invoked)

title: Implement stack auto-detection; inject skills into village_scaffold
description:
## Context

Eliminate the \"mayor must remember to add stack-X skill\" rule by detecting it from the repo.

Detection signals:
| Signal file | Skill |
|---|---|
| \`package.json\` | \`stack-typescript\` |
| \`Anchor.toml\` or \`programs/*/Cargo.toml\` | \`stack-solana\` |
| \`Gemfile\` containing \`rails\` | \`stack-ruby-on-rails\` |
| \`Cargo.toml\` (no Anchor) | \`stack-rust\` (skill defer to follow-up bead) |
| \`go.mod\` | \`stack-go\` (defer) |
| \`pyproject.toml\` / \`requirements.txt\` | \`stack-python\` (defer) |

## Skills

- beads-workflow

title: Implement guard agent: runs all checks (tests/lint/build/coverage)
description:
## Context

\`guard\` is the **terminal mechanical step** in the chain (mayor → worker → inspector → **guard** → envoy?).

Guard runs the heavy machinery: tests, lint, build, type-check, coverage, security scans. Pure tool execution + result reporting. Closes the bead on green; returns to worker on red.

Guard is the only role (besides envoy) allowed to run test suites — worker.md still denies them.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

\`epic/village-v2\`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \`assets/agents/guard.md\` created with frontmatter:
  - tools: bash, read, glob, grep, skill (NO write/edit/webfetch/task)
  - permission.bash: allow tests/lint/build commands; deny push/pull/fetch/branch/merge/rebase/reset; deny \`gh *\`
- [ ] Workflow documented in agent prompt:
  1. \`village_claim\` (assignee=guard) — only picks beads handed off by inspector
  2. Verify the bead has an inspector-pass comment in its history; if not, return to inspector with note (defensive)
  3. Load skills from bead's \`## Skills\`
  4. Checkout the bead's \`## Branch\`
  5. Detect stack and run the stack skill's check matrix (tests + lint + build + typecheck)
  6. Report each check's result via \`br comments add\` with structured table
  7. **Close the bead on green** (\`br close <id> --reason "Checks passed: <summary>"\`) + cascading epic close (preserve current overseer cascade logic)
  8. **Return to worker on red** via \`village_handoff to=worker\` with failing-check details + first error excerpt
  9. **Hand off to envoy** via \`village_invoke specialist=envoy\` ONLY if the bead body explicitly requests a PR/release
- [ ] AGENT_TO_ACTOR map in plugin includes \`guard: "guard"\`
- [ ] \`village_claim\` accepts \`assignee=guard\`
- [ ] Each \`stack-*\` skill updated with explicit \`## Check Matrix\` section listing exact commands

## Notes

Guard is mechanical and terminal. It does not assess scope, AC coverage, or code quality — that's inspector's job (which by then is already done).

A red guard run after a green inspector pass means: the change broke something the inspector couldn't see (runtime/type/build). That always goes back to the worker with full failure context.

title: Implement inspector agent: judgment calls (AC coverage, scope, regressions)
description:
## Context

\`inspector\` is the **first reviewer** in the chain (mayor → worker → **inspector** → guard → envoy?).

Inspector is read-only judgment: assesses what guard can't measure mechanically. Catches scope/AC/regression issues BEFORE guard burns CI cycles on the change.

## Skills

- beads-workflow
- stack-typescript

## Branch

\`epic/village-v2\`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \`assets/agents/inspector.md\` created with frontmatter:
  - tools: bash, read, glob, grep, webfetch, skill (NO write/edit/task; NO test/build commands)
  - permission.bash: allow \`br *\`, \`git diff/log/show/status\`; deny test runners, push, branch ops, \`gh *\`
- [ ] Workflow documented:
  1. \`village_claim\` (assignee=inspector) — picks beads handed off by worker
  2. Load skills + bead's \`## Skills\`
  3. \`git diff\` against bead's branch merge-base
  4. Run **judgment checklist** (output as structured table comment):
     - AC coverage: parse \`- [ ]\` items, verify each is satisfied by the diff, tick them
     - Diff scope: flag files outside expected scope
     - Regression sniff: scan diff for risky patterns (deleted tests, weakened assertions, \`TODO\`/\`console.log\`, hardcoded secrets/URLs, \`unwrap()\`, \`any\` casts)
     - Stack review checklist: each \`stack-*\` skill's \`## Review Checklist\` section
  5. Decide:
     - **Approve judgment** → \`village_handoff to=guard\` with summary of what was checked. Do NOT close — guard closes after mechanical checks.
     - **Changes requested** → \`village_handoff to=worker\` with itemized findings
     - **Out of scope** → \`village_handoff to=mayor\` with explanation
- [ ] Plugin: AGENT_TO_ACTOR includes \`inspector: "inspector"\`; \`village_claim\` accepts \`assignee=inspector\`
- [ ] Each \`stack-*\` skill gains \`## Review Checklist\` section with concrete items
- [ ] DELETE \`assets/agents/overseer.md\` (no backward compat — confirmed)
- [ ] Update \`/village:work\` and \`/village:orphans\` command templates: replace \`overseer\` with \`inspector\` and \`guard\` everywhere
- [ ] Update orphan-fix heuristic in \`/village:orphans\`:
  - keywords \`review|verify|inspect|scope\` → \`inspector\`
  - keywords \`test|lint|build|check\` → \`guard\`
  - default → \`worker\`

## Notes

Inspector NEVER runs tests/builds — it only reads diffs and applies judgment. Guard handles execution after inspector signs off.

Inspector is the gate that prevents misunderstood/over-scoped beads from reaching guard at all.

title: Remove MCP block from opencode.json and create opencode.local.json
description:
## Context

## Context

The tracked `opencode.json` currently has an `"mcp"` block with atlassian and figma servers. This needs to move to a local-only file.

## Skills

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Remove the entire `"mcp": { ... }` block from `opencode.json`
- [ ] Create `opencode.local.json` with the following content:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "atlassian": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp",
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 30000
    },
    "figma": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp",
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 30000
    },
    "coda": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "coda-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "API_KEY": "{env:CODA_API_KEY}"
      },
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```
- [ ] Add `opencode.local.json` to `.gitignore`

## Notes

- Do NOT hardcode any API keys — use `{env:CODA_API_KEY}` variable substitution
- The `.gitignore` currently ignores itself (line 4: `.gitignore`), so just append `opencode.local.json` to it
- OpenCode merges configs: global (`opencode.json`) + custom (`OPENCODE_CONFIG`) — so the split works seamlessly
